title:
Can one AI change
how another AI behaves?
subtitle: A research talk about reading model parameters, editing them, and measuring the consequences.
insights: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming · Takehi, Teoh, Zhang & Khattab · 2 November 2026
A language model reads another network’s numerical parameters and proposes changes.
The authors tested the resulting behavior in games, control tasks and language models.

title: Astra used the task to design a weight change.
subtitle: The source paper connects a behavior, the numbers that produce it, and an intervention.
insights: A trained network is the object being edited. GPT-6 Astra is the editor.
The editor receives the task, the network structure and access to its parameters.
Its output specifies numerical changes to the target network.
Two examples show the idea clearly: a driving policy and a math-solving language model.

title: A stalled car gets a run-up.
subtitle: Astra rewrote a small control path using the car’s position and velocity.
insights: The trained policy drove onto the ramp and stalled.
Back up → accelerate toward the ramp → return control after the jump.
Astra changed 6,073 of 171,664 actor parameters in one response.
The edited policy reached the target in all 1,024 held-out test episodes.

title: A math model kept circling back.
subtitle: Qwen3.5-0.8B often spent its output budget repeating its reasoning.
insights: The task asks the model to solve a math problem and produce a final answer.
In the first diagnostic batch, 85 of 96 answers reached the 32,768-token limit.
Astra compares productive and repetitive contexts to locate the relevant contributions.

title: Reduce the contribution that drives repetition.
subtitle: Astra measured a repetition-related direction and modified the MLP columns writing it.
insights: The direction comes from matched productive and repetitive contexts.
The final edit targets 64 MLP output columns in each of layers 15 and 19.
The source explored intervention strength; its chosen multiplier was 6.
Each selected column has six times its projection along that direction subtracted.

title: More answers reached a useful conclusion.
subtitle: The same source evaluation settings were used before and after the edit.
insights: MATH-500 accuracy rose from 7.9% to 48.1%.
Answers reaching the token limit fell from 93.0% to 33.1%.
The authors’ diagnosis links the gain to reducing repetitive generation.

title: Three questions shaped our experiment.
subtitle: We moved from the source examples to a census classifier, a compact language model and collaborative editing.
insights: RQ1 · Can edits to a lesioned income classifier improve its class-balanced accuracy?
RQ2 · Can bounded edits improve a pretrained language model’s answer selection?
RQ3 · How does feedback-informed collaboration compare with independent editing?

title: Two targets. Four selected models.
subtitle: Each editor starts from the same target. The joint session also receives the independent development histories.
insights: Census classifier: trained here, then lesioned. SmolLM2-1.7B: pretrained and intact.
GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra independently inspect, propose and evaluate patches.
The two models alternate proposal and review across five shared rounds.
Starting model · Sol selection · Astra selection · joint selection.

title: A table of people and an income label.
subtitle: UCI Adult / Census Income predicts annual income above or at most $50,000.
insights: 48,842 records and 14 original feature fields.
Age, education, occupation and weekly hours describe one record.
The label is income above $50,000 or income at most $50,000.

title: We trained the network, then opened an editing stage.
subtitle: Each part of the data served a specific step in the experiment.
insights: 32,561 original training records; 16,281 original test records.
22,792 fit records trained a 104 → 32 → 16 → 1 network with Adam.
The remaining training data supplied lesion calibration, diagnostics and candidate feedback.

title: A weight multiplies a signal.
subtitle: Follow a worked numerical example from two inputs to an income-class decision.
insights: Each incoming signal contributes its input value multiplied by its connection weight.
The contributions and the bias combine into the neuron’s pre-activation.
ReLU passes the positive value onward; the output layer produces a probability.
Change the weight below: every dependent value and the decision update together.

title: We set 16 connection columns to zero.
subtitle: The editing task works on the remaining entries of the second-layer matrix.
insights: The matrix contains 16 destination neurons × 32 incoming connections.
Sixteen input columns are held at zero throughout editing.
The editor sees the remaining learned coefficients and proposes changes to them.

title: Here is what we asked the GPT models to do.
subtitle: A common instruction defines the goal, the information available and the editing actions.
steps: Follow a proposal to its score
insights: Objective: maximize development balanced accuracy on the income-classification task.
Inputs: architecture, weight statistics and a fixed diagnostic panel.
Actions inspect the network, evaluate a complete patch and submit a selected candidate.

title: Add to a few entries. Or scale a column.
subtitle: These two simple operations define the weight changes available to the editors.
insights: A sparse addition changes explicitly named matrix entries.
Column scaling multiplies all entries of selected columns by a factor.
The evaluator applies the candidate to the starting weights and returns its development score.

title: Sol selected sixteen different additions.
subtitle: The stored patch changes row 0 of the second-layer weight matrix.
insights: All sixteen entries feed the same destination neuron.
The selected additions have different magnitudes, including +0.0315, +0.0518 and +0.0280.
The same patch is then applied across every record in the final evaluation.

title: Astra selected +0.003 on each of sixteen entries.
subtitle: Its recorded search compared several step sizes on the development panel.
insights: The search tried positive, negative and smaller positive additions.
Both +0.005 and +0.003 reached the same best recorded development balanced accuracy.
The selection rule chose the smaller +0.003 change.

title: Proposal → review → measurement → next round.
subtitle: The joint session uses both independent histories and alternates the two GPT roles.
insights: The history contains previous patches and their development scores.
GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra alternate proposer and reviewer.
One reviewed patch is measured per round; its score becomes shared feedback.
The selected Adult joint delta equals 0.93 × Sol’s selected delta at all sixteen entries.

title: One stored coefficient, three edits.
subtitle: Compare the selected values for connection [0, 15], then multiply by the same activation.
insights: The original coefficient is approximately 0.12482.
Astra adds 0.003 to this entry.
Sol adds 0.028 to this entry.
The joint patch adds 0.02604: 93% of Sol’s addition.

title: A small probability shift can cross the decision threshold.
subtitle: These are saved predictions for two held-out records.
insights: Both starting probabilities lie just below the 0.5 decision threshold.
The edited probabilities rise to 0.50948 and 0.50781.
One decision becomes correct; the other becomes incorrect.

title: 65 recovered decisions. 102 newly incorrect decisions.
subtitle: For Sol’s selected patch, the changes occur in different income classes.
insights: 65 higher-income records move from incorrect to correct.
102 lower-income records move from correct to incorrect.
The test set contains 3,846 higher-income and 12,435 lower-income records.

title: The two accuracy metrics weight records differently.
subtitle: Ordinary accuracy counts records equally. Balanced accuracy averages the two class recalls.
insights: The net change is 65 − 102 = −37 correct records.
The higher-income and lower-income class rates change by different amounts.
Their equally weighted average gives +0.4349 percentage points of balanced accuracy.

title: The class-balanced score increased.
subtitle: Held-out evaluation of the four selected models · 16,281 records.
insights: Sol: +0.4349 pp. Joint: +0.3810 pp. Astra: approximately unchanged.
The paired intervals quantify example uncertainty for these selected models.
Ordinary accuracy and probability quality moved in the opposite direction for Sol and joint.

title: The joint selection finished close to Sol.
subtitle: The endpoint comparison links the cooperative outcome to the independent benchmark.
insights: Sol: 79.0207% balanced accuracy. Joint: 78.9668%.
Joint − Sol: −0.0539 pp; paired 95% interval −0.1260 to +0.0062 pp.
This seed compares ten-slot solo searches with five joint rounds using earlier feedback.

title: The second target answers multiple-choice questions.
subtitle: SmolLM2-1.7B starts from its pretrained weights.
insights: ARC-Easy tests school-science questions; PIQA tests physical commonsense.
Each candidate answer is scored as a continuation of the question.
The selected answer is determined by the benchmark’s likelihood-scoring rule.

title: A clear objective and a bounded part of the model.
subtitle: Both GPT editors receive the same language-model task and the same permitted operations.
steps: Read the feedback and selection rule
insights: Objective: maximize development ARC-Easy acc_norm.
Editable weights: MLP output matrices; operations: column scaling and sparse additions.
Inspect train diagnostics, propose a complete patch, read its score, then select a candidate.

title: One proposal halved 32 output columns.
subtitle: A recorded candidate in transformer layer 23 changes the contribution of selected MLP features.
insights: The output matrix combines the MLP’s internal features into the layer output.
Columns 0–31 are selected by the stored operation.
65,536 actual coefficients change in this candidate.
Development acc_norm remains 75.00%, matching the starting score.

chapter: RQ2 · HOW THE SCORE IS COMPUTED
title: Each answer receives a likelihood score.
subtitle: A worked example shows the same scoring rule used by the benchmark.
insights: The model supplies a continuation log-likelihood for each answer.
acc_norm divides by the answer text’s character count.
The highest normalized score selects the answer; comparison with the key gives correctness.

title: The search selected the original weights.
subtitle: Five candidate attempts per independent editor; five joint attempts.
insights: The best development score remains 75.00%.
The original model has the smallest change size among tied candidates.
The single selected weight state scores 73.44% on ARC-Easy and 78.52% on PIQA.

title: Three questions. Three measured answers.
subtitle: The experiment connects proposed edits to actual weights, decisions and outcomes.
insights: RQ1 · Direct edits improved class-balanced accuracy while shifting the distribution of errors.
RQ2 · Bounded search selected SmolLM2’s original state on these tasks.
RQ3 · The joint endpoint stayed close to the strongest independent endpoint.

title: Make the next intervention more informative.
subtitle: Use what this experiment revealed to choose the next experiments.
insights: Use activation-guided directions and richer candidate spaces to target specific behavior.
Evaluate class-balanced gains alongside error costs and probability quality.
Compare equal-budget histories and multiple independent sessions to isolate collaboration effects.
